newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market sees subdued start to week.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market sees subdued start to week.

text.p: Business was subdued on the sugar freight market on Monday and shipbrokers continued to complain of low rates and the scarcity of fresh inquiry.
But they said orders were likely to pick up soon after the expiry of New York's October raw sugar contract, when physical deliveries of cargoes would become known.
Expected origins are north Brazil and possibly some central American producer nations, they said.
Of Monday's new business, E D & F Man quoted for 12/14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Natal and Cabadelo/Recife to Tema and Lagos for prompt dates.
Man also repeated its recent bulk order from Paranagua to Algeria/Black Sea.
Iranian shippers IRISL issued an account order for 14,000 tonnes min/max preslung bagged sugar from Antwerp-Hamburg range excluding the U.K. to Iran for October 15/30.
Louis Dreyfus repeated its earlier Santos/Aqaba inquiry.
